title: P1 — Port-range allocator leak: non-force destroy returns not_found after userdel failure WITHOUT freeing the range; TTL-expired agents exhausted the whole las-03 pool (proven 2026-09-03)
detail: PROVEN LIVE on bunker-las-03 (imhotep foreman tick T230, 2026-09-03 ~19:45Z): after the fleet-wide 17:11Z bunkerd restart, audit export shows 19 successful SpawnAgent vs 9 ok DestroyAgent + 15 not_found DestroyAgent → 19−9 = 10 = the ENTIRE pool (config port_range 30000-31000, 100/agent) held by agent IDs invisible to the registry. ListAgents = 0 agents while SpawnAgent failed 26x with 'port range allocation: no free port ranges available (pool exhausted: 10 ranges)' from 18:15Z to 19:48Z (QA spawn bursts 19:10-19:19Z + retries). Host also shows 48 bunker-* users persisting (many with RUNNING rootless dockerd processes) while the registry lists none. ROOT CAUSE CHAIN: internal/agent/manager_destroy.go Step 3 (~:63-73) — non-force destroy where userdel -rf fails (agent user still owns running processes: rootless dockerd/rootlesskit daemons) does m.tracker.Unregister(agentID) and returns Status not_found WITHOUT calling m.portAlloc.Free(agentID); Free only runs at ~:115 after full cleanup. The TTL reaper (manager.go reapExpiredAgents, 1-min ticker → Destroy non-force) is a frequent triggering caller: expired agent whose rootless dockerd didn't die in time → userdel fails → registry slot freed, port range leaked forever (allocator is in-memory; restart clears it, orphan users/daemons do NOT clear). Secondary defect: Step 1 dockerd stop (stopDockerdDirect + systemctl --user fallback) never WAITS for the rootlesskit/dockerd PIDs to actually exit before userdel -rf runs. FIX SKETCH: (1) call m.portAlloc.Free(agentID) in the not_found early-return path — unconditional, idempotent (Free no-ops for unknown IDs); (2) harden Step 1: after stop, poll up to ~10s for the agent user's rootlesskit/dockerd PIDs to exit, SIGKILL stragglers, then userdel; (3) same Free-before-return guarantee on any other early return between Allocate and the final Free. PASS: (1) unit test — non-force destroy with failing userdel returns not_found AND portAlloc.Available() is back to full; (2) unit test — force-mode destroy with failing userdel still frees; (3) TTL-reaper path covered — expired agent with a running process does not leak a range; (4) existing suite green; VERIFY-PASS evidence committed. OPS NOTE (not part of PASS): after fix deploys, las-03 needs a steward/Bane root pass to restart bunkerd (reclaims the 10 leaked ranges — sudo restart is approval-blocked in cron sessions) and to clean the 48 orphan bunker-* users + their dockerd daemons. Detection recipe for recurrence: bunker audit export → compare ok-spawn count vs ok-destroy count since last restart; delta > 0 = leaked ranges.

title: [P1] bunker-qa.sh spawn_agent retry loop leaks the attempt-1 agent when attempt 1 spawns server-side but returns unparseable output — run destroyed a different agent ID than it spawned; cleanup() also swallows destroy failures with || true
detail: LIVE 2026-09-15 (dogfood REAL tick targeting bunker, server bunker-las-02, run /tmp/dagger-role-qa-2259038-1789510605536506949): run.log cleanup line says 'destroying temp agent 0ecbb9e8', but `bunker list --server bunker-las-02` after the run showed agent 230abb5b STILL RUNNING with creation timestamp inside the run's spawn window (2026-09-15T15:18:54-07:00). Mechanism: spawn_agent() (bunker-qa.sh:32-45) loops 3x on `bunker spawn` output parsing (`grep -oP 'keys/\K[a-f0-9]+'`); a spawn that SUCCEEDS server-side (agent user created) but whose output fails to parse (CLI warning/mixed output) makes attempt 2 spawn a SECOND agent while the first is orphaned — BUNKER_QA_AGENT is set only after the loop succeeds, so cleanup() (bunker-qa.sh:384) destroys only the last agent; the TTL is the only backstop for the leak. Secondary: cleanup() pipes `bunker destroy ... || true`, so a failed destroy is never surfaced (destroy-failure escalation contract from the bunker-agent-isolation skill is defeated). Found and destroyed manually same day (`bunker destroy 230abb5b` rc=0, server back to 1 agent). Fix direction: (a) capture ALL ids parsed across spawn attempts and destroy non-selected ones before proceeding, or fail the run; (b) log + emit a FAIL/INFO evidence cell when `bunker destroy` exits non-zero instead of || true; (c) optional post-destroy verify: re-list and assert the id is gone.

MECHANISM (code-traced in internal/audit/ship.go): run() pops the drained item and computes depth=len(s.queue) while holding s.mu, then RELEASES the lock and only afterwards calls writeState() (ship.go:366-368) — the persisted shipstate therefore still carries the PREVIOUS attempt's snapshot (ok/queue_depth 1) at the instant a reader observes the drained in-memory snapshot; ship_test.go's drain loop breaks on the in-memory snapshot() and then reads the state FILE once, with no convergence deadline, so the file assertion (line ~280) races the state write. FIX DIRECTION: publish the state file from the same critical section that publishes the queue depth (or serialize state writes and derive depth from the live queue instead of a caller-supplied value), then make the test assert FILE convergence with a bounded deadline instead of a single read after an in-memory drain. title: [P2] bunker mount fails reproducibly against a healthy agent with raw 'read: Connection reset by peer' — no retry, no actionable error
detail: On bunker-las-04 with agent df0916a (running, exec + docker + tunnel all healthy): `bunker mount df0916a /mnt` failed 2/2 times with `read: Connection reset by peer` + `bunker: sshfs failed: exit status 1`. title: [P1] Every bunker-* SSH session on the demo host is DENIED (pam_open_session: System error) — exec/mount/cp are all broken against healthy, running agents; the provisioned GAP-075 PAM block demands a group membership the stale deployed daemon never grants
detail: LIVE (foreman tick 439, bunker-mvp, agent foreman-vrf-1789573645 — spawned and registered as RUNNING by the deployed daemon). SYMPTOM: ssh to the agent returns exit status 254 with the login banner as the only output and NO command output; sshfs reports 'remote host has disconnected' / 'read: Connection reset by peer'. sshd journal per connection: 'pam_unix(sshd:session): session opened for user bunker-<id>(uid=1010)' then 'error: PAM: pam_open_session(): System error'. The daemon's flagship workflow (exec over SSH, mount, cp) therefore cannot work on the demo host at all while the daemon reports the agent running. ROOT CAUSE, ONE COMMAND: /etc/pam.d/sshd carries the GAP-075 block — classifier `pam_succeed_if user !~ bunker-*`, then `[success=ignore default=die] pam_exec.so quiet /usr/lib/bunker/pam-tmp-guard verify bunker-agents`, then `required pam_namespace.so`. `PAM_USER=<fresh agent> /usr/lib/bunker/pam-tmp-guard verify bunker-agents` → 'bunker-pam-guard: user <id> is not a member of bunker-agents', rc=1 → pam_exec maps non-zero to PAM_SYSTEM_ERR → `default=die` denies the session. An OLDER agent that is in the group passes (PAM_USER=bunker-imgspec-none → rc=0) and its SSH works, so the discriminator is GROUP MEMBERSHIP, not agent health. Host has the SSH-side provision (drop-in + helper dated 2026-09-13) while /opt/bunker/bunkerd is the 2026-08-30 build that predates the spawn-side 'isolation-provision' stage that adds new agents to bunker-agents — host provisioned, daemon too old = every agent that daemon spawns is locked out of SSH. FIX: (1) restore congruence — deploy the HEAD daemon to the demo so spawn grants the membership (this is the DF-BUNKER-10 lag class and it must happen before ANY live exec/mount verification on the demo can be trusted); or `bunker host-provision --uninstall --apply` to return to shared /tmp — never hand-delete only the drop-in, whose own comment warns that the remaining pam_exec precondition then fails closed and locks EVERY bunker-* session out; (2) make the skew impossible — host-provision refuses (or loudly warns) when the installed daemon is older than the hardening it installs, and spawn grants the membership BEFORE the agent is reported ready; (3) operator-facing — `bunker exec` surfaces the session-denial cause instead of a bare exit 254. PASS: (1) a freshly spawned agent on the demo host accepts `bunker exec <id> -- whoami` with real output (no 254) and `bunker mount <id>` succeeds; (2) a test proves the provision/daemon version-skew check rejects an older daemon; (3) spawn reports ready only after an SSH exec probe succeeds. RELATED / REFUTES: DF-BUNKER-14 (mount fails against a healthy agent) blames the CLI's fixed `-o allow_other`; that is REFUTED live — sshfs with allow_other AND without it fail identically against the same agent, the raw SFTP channel is clean (.hushlogin changes nothing), and a plain `ssh` to that agent already fails with 254.

reasoning.note: Found while verifying DF-BUNKER-14's premise live. The chain a later tick must not re-derive: the sshd PAM journal line, the one-command guard reproduction, and the membership discriminator between a locked-out fresh agent and a working older one. Filed separately from DF-BUNKER-14 so the mount row closes against the right root cause instead of an allow_other fallback that fixes nothing.

Failed to connect to bus: No medium found'. title: [P1] Standalone E2E gate takes over the live daemon and ports (nested regression suite pkills bunkerd, rebinds :18080/:19090 and deletes the operator CLI config) and its section-12 nested verdict is vacuous
detail: [P1] Standalone E2E gate cannot reach VERIFY-PASS on a host with a systemd-managed daemon: the nested regression suite takes over the live ports (pkill bunkerd + its own daemon on :18080/:19090) and DELETES the operator CLI config, and section 12's nested verdict is vacuous. MEASURED (foreman tick 450, bunker-mvp, HEAD 1872d22, /usr/local/bin binaries certified MATCH): `BUNKER_TOKEN=<daemon token> BUNKER_DAEMON_URL=http://localhost:18080 BUNKERD_REST_ADDR=:18080 BUNKERD_GRPC_ADDR=:19090 bash e2e-full-battery.sh` -> Pass 111 / Fail 4 -> VERIFY-FAIL. Red cells: (1) section 13 'allowed spec spawn failed - Creating agent... bunker: spawn agent: unavailable: dial tcp [::1]:18080: connect: connection refused'; (2) section 13 'jq NOT found in agent image - agent "e2e-imgspec" not found' (cascade of 1); (3) section 14 'destroy of a never-seen ID unexpectedly succeeded'; (4) 'OPERATOR CLI CONFIG MODIFIED BY THIS RUN - /root/.bunker/config.yaml before sha256:f4098a0b3d594434... after ABSENT'. Host journal at the same minute: bunkerd[2139762] shutting down signal=terminated 13:43:17Z -> systemd 'Started bunkerd.service' 13:43:24 -> 'bunkerd: server error: listen tcp :18080: bind: address already in use' 13:43:25 -> started again 13:43:27 (systemctl show bunkerd -p NRestarts -> 4). Linger 73 -> 74 (one stale entry left by the run; pruned afterwards with the deployed `bunker linger prune`, kept 1 live). MECHANISM (two independent harness defects, standalone path only): (A) TAKEOVER COLLISION - e2e-full-battery.sh section 12 invokes the nested suite in standalone mode WITHOUT dedicated ports (the else branch ~line 1351), so regression-tests.sh inherits the battery's exported BUNKERD_REST_ADDR=:18080 / BUNKERD_GRPC_ADDR=:19090, runs `pkill bunkerd` (line 111; again at cleanup line 91), starts its OWN daemon on those production ports with a temp auth-disabled config (line 156), and line 122 does `rm -rf /root/.bunker /run/bunker/* /etc/bunkerd/ssh/*` - i.e. it destroys exactly the operator CLI state that INT-CI-010's isolation work exists to protect. The systemd unit auto-restarts and races the nested daemon for :18080, so the production daemon is unavailable exactly when sections 13/14 dial it. (B) VACUOUS NESTED VERDICT - `REG_EXIT=$?` (~line 1353) reads the status of the surrounding if-block and the command substitution ends with `|| true`, so REG_EXIT is ALWAYS 0: the battery asserts 'regression suite PASSED' even though the nested suite printed 'PASS: 16 / FAIL: 14'. REG_PASS/REG_FAIL are naive `grep -c PASS/FAIL` counts of the transcript words, not the nested suite's tally. A nested suite that dies is therefore invisible. FIX DIRECTION: (1) give the nested suite its own isolated ports in standalone mode (coexist already uses :29092/:28082) and make regression-tests.sh refuse to `pkill bunkerd` when a systemd-managed production daemon is active, stopping only the daemon it started itself; (2) never `rm -rf` operator CLI state - run the nested suite with its own BUNKER_HOME/HOME and remove only that throwaway dir, gating the /run/bunker + /etc/bunkerd/ssh sweeps on daemon ownership; (3) capture the nested exit status without `|| true` masking it and FAIL the battery (not `note`) on a non-zero nested exit, counting the nested suite's own tally lines; (4) sections 13/14 must probe daemon reachability and name the endpoint before cascading 'not found' cells; (5) README states the standalone contract. PASS: (a) --self-test PASS incl. new assertions (nested suite gets non-production ports in standalone; a nested suite exiting 1 flips section 12 to a failure; the battery never removes a config it did not create); (b) grep-provable: no unconditional `pkill bunkerd` reachable while a systemd-managed daemon is active, no `rm -rf` of the operator config dir; (c) --show-plan/--bin-report unchanged; (d) live standalone gate on bunker-mvp prints 0 FAIL / VERIFY-PASS with the production daemon uptime continuous (NRestarts unchanged) and /root/.bunker/config.yaml's sha256 unchanged; (e) coexist path unchanged (CI stays green).

title: [P1] spawn fails at rootless-install when the allocated uid is recycled (previous owner's user@<uid> manager still active -> session-bus daemon-reload fails) and the failed-spawn rollback leaks the linger entry
detail: [P1] spawn dies at stage rootless-install whenever the freshly allocated uid was RECYCLED from an agent whose systemd user manager is still live, and the failed-spawn rollback leaks the linger entry. MEASURED (foreman tick 450, bunker-mvp, HEAD 1872d22, deployed daemon 0.1.4/1872d22): the standalone E2E gate's nested regression suite ran 14 red cells, ALL cascade from one spawn. The daemon's own attribution (/var/log/bunkerd-regression.log): 'spawn entering stage regr-alpha stage=rootless-install' -> WARN 'agent user manager unreachable from the agent session before the rootless install' user=bunker-regr-alpha unit=user@1002.service state='unit user@1002.service: is-active=active (Result=success)' linger_entries=3 -> WARN 'userdel failed; terminating user processes and retrying' error='userdel bunker-regr-alpha: exit status 8 (output: userdel: user bunker-regr-alpha is currently used by process 2168325)' -> ERROR 'spawn failed stage=rootless-install error=... daemon-reload through the session bus failed; unit user@1002.service: is-active=active (Result=success); linger entries: 3'. uid 1002 had been used minutes earlier by a destroyed agent in the same gate run (foreman-idemo-*), and systemctl showed user@1002.service still ACTIVE at spawn time (it only went 'failed (Result: signal)' when the rollback killed it). SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME PATH: the rollback of a failed spawn does NOT un-linger - after the run /var/lib/systemd/linger held bunker-regr-alpha, bunker-1dd412d0 and bunker-ff86d69a while none of those users existed (the destroy path DOES un-linger, proven tick 441; the failed-spawn rollback path apparently does not). All three were pruned with the deployed `bunker linger prune` (scanned 4, stale removed 3, kept 1 live). WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: the pre-INT-CI-012 harness printed 'regression suite PASSED' over the nested suite's 'PASS: 16 / FAIL: 14' (see INT-CI-012). FIX DIRECTION: (1) in the rootless-install stage, treat an ACTIVE user manager for the allocated uid as a live signal, not a failure: the reachability probe's `systemctl --user daemon-reload` must not fail the spawn when user@<uid>.service is active for a DIFFERENT (recycled) user name - either assert the runtime dir/bus belongs to the agent's own user before probing, or retry after resetting the stale manager for that uid; (2) never allocate a uid whose user manager is still active (or stop/terminate it as part of spawn's fresh-uid preparation); (3) make the failed-spawn rollback un-linger exactly like destroy does. PASS: (a) a test proves spawn succeeds (or fails with an attribution naming the recycled uid) when the allocated uid's previous user manager is still active; (b) a live repro on the demo host: spawn an agent, destroy it, immediately spawn again (uid recycled) -> spawn completes; (c) `ls /var/lib/systemd/linger` is unchanged across a FAILED spawn (rollback un-lingers); (d) the nested regression suite's 14 spawn/exec/list cells go green in the standalone gate.
reasoning: Surfaced by the live standalone gate AFTER INT-CI-012's harness fix restored an honest nested verdict: the 14 red cells were previously reported as 'regression suite PASSED'. The attribution comes from the daemon's own breadcrumb (stage + unit state + userdel conflict + linger count), not from a guess, and the uid was demonstrably recycled inside one gate run.

title: [P1] The recycled-uid recovery (1d1fb4c) fires but does not recover: after its one-shot teardown+bring-up the agent session still cannot reach user@<recycled-uid>.service, so spawn keeps dying at stage rootless-install and the standalone gate's nested regression suite stays at PASS=16 / FAIL=14
detail: [P1] MEASURED tick 452 on bunker-mvp with the deployed HEAD 8aa4d8a (the daemon carries the INT-SPAWN-001 fix 1d1fb4c): the standalone gate's nested regression suite (its OWN daemon on 127.0.0.1:29092, isolated ports per the INT-CI-012 fix) still fails spawn at the rootless-install stage, and the NEW recovery path runs and STILL loses. Daemon log /var/log/bunkerd-regression.log, 15:41:13-15:41:16Z, verbatim: (1) 15:41:13.488 INFO 'spawn entering stage' agent_id=regr-alpha stage=rootless-install; (2) 15:41:13.882 WARN 'agent user manager unreachable from the agent session before the rootless install' user=bunker-regr-alpha unit=user@1002.service state='unit user@1002.service: is-active=active (Result=success)' linger_entries=6 journal='...docker.service: Failed with result exit-code...'; (3) 15:41:13.937 WARN 'recycled-uid recovery: the unit is ACTIVE but the agent session cannot reach the manager; tearing the foreign manager down and bringing the manager up again' uid=1002; (4) 15:41:14.763 WARN the same unreachable message again; (5) 15:41:14.976 ERROR 'spawn failed ... rootless-install: agent user manager unreachable before the rootless install ... daemon-reload through the session bus failed; unit user@1002.service: is-active=active (Result=success); linger entries: 6; journal: <new manager startup lines>; recycled-uid recovery was attempted once (user@1002.service torn down and brought back up) and the agent session still cannot reach the manager'. The same sequence repeated for the next spawn (agent_id=42a1b1e1, uid 1002, 15:41:15.8-15:41:16.8). TIMING: the whole recovery (teardown + bring-up + final probe) fits in ~0.83s (13.937 -> 14.763) and the final probe fails ~30ms after the second WARN - consistent with a bus/manager that is not yet serving the agent session when the final probe runs, but the artifact cannot prove it because the probe's own error text is DISCARDED. DIAGNOSABILITY GAP (fix this first, it is one line): proveUserManagerReachableErr (internal/agent/rootless.go:418) formats '... daemon-reload through the session bus failed; %s; linger entries: %d; journal: %s' from the unit state, the linger count and the journal excerpt - the probe's own error (returned by userSessionRunner, i.e. the actual systemctl/su stderr) is dropped, so every live occurrence names the symptom set but never the cause. Include the probe error in the attribution and in the recovery's final error, then re-run the standalone gate and read the real cause. CONTRAST THAT MAKES THIS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT A MISDIAGNOSIS: on the SAME host, minutes earlier, the PRODUCTION daemon (same binary) spawned an agent on a recycled uid 1002 whose previous owner's manager was still ACTIVE - `systemctl show user@1002.service -p ActiveState` = active/SubState running after the destroy - and that spawn completed with NO recovery WARN at all (plain stages rootless-install -> dockerd-start -> session-probe, rc 0, exec rc 0). So the probe CAN succeed against an active foreign manager; it fails in the nested-suite context. Candidate causes worth measuring first: (a) the final probe runs on a su-login session whose XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS point at a runtime dir the recovery just recreated (stale bus inode vs new socket), (b) the bring-up returns before the user manager's bus socket is actually accepting (a bounded connectivity wait, not a fixed budget), (c) linger churn (linger_entries 6, one entry was held for a live agent at that moment) starving the manager start. PASS: (1) the attribution error carries the probe's own stderr; (2) a controlled repro on the demo host (or the nested suite) shows the recovery actually recovering - the second probe succeeds and the spawn completes on a recycled uid in that context; (3) the standalone gate's nested regression suite reports 0 FAIL (its 14 red cells go green); (4) the fix does not weaken the healthy path (no destructive call when the first probe succeeds) and adds at most one bounded wait.

title: [P1] spawn dies at rootless-install with 'Failed to connect to bus: No medium found' because the readiness gate is a socket-file stat, not a bus handshake: the manager is up (is-active=active, dbus.socket Listening) while the agent session cannot connect
detail: [P1] MEASURED tick 453 on bunker-mvp with the INT-SPAWN-002 fix deployed (87aa282 applied to /opt/bunker, rebuilt, installed, bunkerd restarted): the standalone nested suite still reports PASS=16 / FAIL=14 and EVERY red cell is a spawn that dies at stage rootless-install. The new attribution (INT-SPAWN-002 C1) names the real error for the first time, verbatim: session_probe='Failed to connect to bus: No medium found' with unit user@1002.service is-active=active (Result=success) and linger_entries=8. Journal for the same second (16:10:25-16:10:27Z) shows the manager coming up cleanly - 'Starting user@1002.service', 'Listening on dbus.socket', 'systemctl --user set-environment DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1002/bus' - then the su session (pam_unix(su-l:session) opened and closed) fails with ENOMEDIUM 0.7s later, the recovery stops the unit, a NEW manager starts, and the SECOND probe fails with the same error. The one-shot recovery therefore runs to completion and the failure reproduces immediately after it. NOT THE MECHANISM (disproved by controlled probes on the production daemon the same tick): (a) same-name uid recycling alone - spawn/destroy/spawn of tick453-alpha reused uid 1002 and succeeded twice with exec OK; (b) an ACTIVE manager for a deleted account - spawn tick453-beta, userdel -rf only (user@1003 is-active=active, logind record gone), spawn tick453-gamma on the recycled uid 1003 succeeded with exec OK. The stale-logind-record WARN of INT-SPAWN-002 did NOT fire during the failing run. LEADING HYPOTHESIS (not yet proven): waitForUserManager only polls os.Stat(<runtimeDir>/bus) - it returns as soon as the socket PATH exists, which is not evidence that the bus accepts a connection; in the failing runs the probe arrives ~0.7s after a fresh manager start and libdbus answers ENOMEDIUM. title: [P1] `su -` RESETS the session environment, so userSessionEnv's XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS never reach the agent session: the probe gets NEITHER variable and systemctl answers 'Failed to connect to bus: No medium found' - a PERMANENT condition in any daemon not launched by systemd (the standalone gate's nested suite), not the readiness race INT-SPAWN-003 assumed
detail: [P1] MEASURED tick 454 on bunker-mvp (78.46.173.180) with the INT-SPAWN-003 fix deployed (a499216 installed to /usr/local/bin/bunker+bunkerd, nested regression suite run standalone on its own ports, log /tmp/tick454-nested.log, daemon log /var/log/bunkerd-regression.log). The nested suite is STILL PASS=16 / FAIL=14 and every red cell is a spawn dying at stage rootless-install. The new readiness wait proves the condition is PERMANENT rather than a late-answering bus: 16:38:09.324Z INFO retry line (first probe refused, session_probe='Failed to connect to bus: No medium found', unit user@1002.service is-active=active), 16:38:39.387Z the FULL-30s-budget exhaustion WARN + one-shot recycled-uid recovery, 16:38:40.167Z the recovery's own readiness wait starts and burns ANOTHER 30s (16:39:10.204Z final attribution, same error). ~60s of probing across a manager teardown+bring-up without a single successful answer. ROOT CAUSE, PROVEN BY CONTROLLED PROBES THIS TICK (all commands run as root on the host): (1) `su -` RESETS THE ENVIRONMENT - `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1002 DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1002/bus su - kara -c 'echo XDG=[$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR] DBUS=[$DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS]'` prints `XDG=[] DBUS=[]`, so the env userSessionEnv sets on the `su` process (internal/agent/rootless.go userSessionEnv, called by runUserSessionCmd/runRootlessInstallerCmd) is STRIPPED before the probe runs - the file comment claiming the values are 'layered on top of the inherited environment' and 'the installer call uses the SAME construction' is factually wrong for `su -`; (2) the EXACT error text is the no-variable case - `env -u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS -u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR systemctl --user daemon-reload` on the same host prints verbatim 'Failed to connect to bus: No medium found'; (3) IN-BAND injection works - `su - kara -c "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1002 DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1002/bus sh -c 'echo \$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR'"` prints `/run/user/1002`; (4) the CONTRAST that makes this host-context-dependent: the systemd-launched production daemon on this same host (env carries NEITHER variable) spawns agents successfully, and the host journal records NO pam_systemd 'New session ... of user bunker-<id>' line for the failing su calls (only pam_unix su-l session open/close), so no login stack provides the bus address in that context either - the mechanism behind the contrast (why pam_systemd registers no session for the su child in the non-systemd case) is the ONE thing still unmeasured. FIX DIRECTION: stop relying on the su process environment - build the session environment INSIDE the command the session runs (e.g. `su - <user> -c 'XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=<dir> DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=<dir>/bus systemctl --user daemon-reload'`, or a `env ... sh -c` wrapper) for the probe, the daemon-reload retry AND the rootless installer call, keeping one shared construction so INT-CI-009's 'same env for every user-session command' property becomes TRUE instead of aspirational; add a live-faithful unit test that fails against a runner which sets cmd.Env only. PASS: (1) the nested suite's spawn cells go green on the demo host (the 14 red cells clear; tally PASS=30 / FAIL=0) OR a controlled repro shows the probe succeeding in the non-systemd daemon context; (2) a unit test proves the session command carries the bus address in-band and the probe no longer depends on pam_systemd setting anything; (3) the healthy production path is unchanged (probe succeeds, zero destructive calls, one probe when the bus answers immediately); (4) go build/vet/test/gofmt clean. EVIDENCE: /var/log/bunkerd-regression.log 16:38:08-16:39:13Z on bunker-mvp, the four controlled probes above, /tmp/tick454-nested.log. MECHANISM MEASURED (same tick, two probes on the host, 16:48Z): running the SAME su from a logind session vs from a non-session context flips pam_systemd's behaviour. (A) from the ssh login session that launches the standalone gate: `su - kara -c 'echo XDG=[$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR] DBUS=[$DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS]'` -> `XDG=[] DBUS=[]` (no bus address); (B) the production-daemon shape, a transient service outside any logind session: `systemd-run --quiet --wait --pipe --unit=tick454-probe su - kara -c ...` -> `XDG=[/run/user/1001] DBUS=[unix:path=/run/user/1001/bus]`. pam_systemd therefore sets the bus environment for the su session ONLY when the calling process is not already inside a logind session; when the daemon descends from an ssh login session it provides nothing, and because `su -` strips the caller's environment the agent session ends up with NEITHER variable. That is why the production systemd daemon and the CI runner (both services, no logind session) spawn fine while the ssh-launched standalone gate fails 100% - the same binary, the same host, a different launch context. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: the session bus environment must be built IN-BAND (inside the command the session runs) and must never depend on pam_systemd or on the su process environment; probe (3) above already proves the in-band form reaches the child.

title: [P1] build-and-test / Unit tests is RED on a board-only commit (run 35253802213, sha 58546f5): TestServerInfo fails its own UptimeSeconds guard (service_test.go:702) with a mechanism the guard cannot explain, and the same internal/server run makes a REAL public-CA call to acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org for bunker.example.com (rejectedIdentifier) - the other three CI jobs skip on `needs`, so each such flake costs a whole push its coverage
detail: [P1] The Tier-0 CI job `build-and-test` FAILED at step 'Unit tests' on a BOARD-ONLY commit, so the other three jobs (regression, root-suite, gitreins-guard) were SKIPPED by `needs` and the push got zero coverage. EVIDENCE (GitHub run 35253802213, repo deployBunker/bunker, headSha 58546f5, created 2026-09-17T17:36:49Z - board JSONL + .gitreins/tasks.yaml only, no .go change): `gh run view ... --json jobs` = build-and-test failure (failed step 'Unit tests'), regression/root-suite/gitreins-guard skipped. FAILED ASSERTION, verbatim: `--- FAIL: TestServerInfo (0.00s)` / `service_test.go:702: ServerInfo().UptimeSeconds is 0, want seconds since daemon start` / `FAIL github.com/deployBunker/bunker/internal/server 1.019s` - the ONLY red in the run. WHY THE GUARD DOES NOT EXPLAIN IT: the assertion is `if msg.UptimeSeconds == 0 && time.Since(serverStartTime) >= time.Second` (internal/server/service_test.go:701) and both sides read the same package var `serverStartTime = time.Now()` (internal/server/service.go:37) via `uint64(time.Since(serverStartTime).Seconds())` (service.go:97). With elapsed >= 1s the value cannot be 0, and with elapsed < 1s the test must NOT fail - so this is NOT a simple razor-edge flake as the comment above it asserts ('CI: UHLP-145 razor-edge pattern; bunker FLAKE-001'). The mechanism is UNKNOWN as of filing and must be reproduced before it is fixed; the observable fact is that the same tree's Go tests passed in run 35251913868 (sha 95e55a8, 18 minutes earlier, build-and-test success) and in the foreman's local `go test ./... -count=1` on this tick (internal/server ok 1.293s). SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT VISIBLE IN THE SAME LOG: during the internal/server package run the test binary made a REAL public-CA call - `info done waiting on internal rate limiter {"identifiers": ["bunker.example.com"], "ca": "https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory"}`, `info using ACME account .../acct/3760420716`, then `error obtain could not get certificate from issuer ... urn:ietf:params:acme:error:rejectedIdentifier - Cannot issue for bunker.example.com: forbidden by policy`. certmagic's async obtain for bunker.example.com escapes the test-side CA override (TestBuildTLSConfig_AutoTLSProducesConfig points certmagic.DefaultACME.CA at https://127.0.0.1:14000/dir and restores it in t.Cleanup, so a background obtain that starts after cleanup uses the REAL production CA). A unit test must never contact a public CA: it is nondeterministic, it depends on runner network egress, and here it produced a 400 from Let's Encrypt's policy check. FIX DIRECTION: (1) reproduce the uptime failure deterministically (run the package with `-count=20` and `-race` on CI-like hardware; print serverStartTime and time.Since(serverStartTime) inside the failing assertion to settle whether the var is being mutated or the elapsed measurement is the liar) and then fix the assertion so it can only fail for a real cause; (2) isolate certmagic in unit tests - for EVERY test that builds an auto_tls config, point certmagic.DefaultACME.CA at a local ACME test server for the WHOLE test lifetime (or set a certmagic config that never starts an async obtain) and assert the test made zero calls to acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org; (3) consider making the Tier-0 job's job-level conclusion the CI gate rather than the run-level one, so a single flaky unit test does not silently skip the regression + root-suite coverage.
reasoning: Filed because a Tier-0 red on an unrelated commit silently skips regression + root-suite + gitreins-guard for that push (scheduled jobs are gated on `needs: build-and-test`), so it hides far more than it shows, and because the ACME observation is a second defect of the same class (unit tests with live external dependencies) that no row owns. The commit that tripped it changed only board JSONL, so nothing in this row is attributable to that change.
review_notes: No product behaviour change needed for the fix (test isolation + assertion hardening); the live E2E battery is NOT required (AGENTS.md gate 3 covers spawn/destroy/exec/docker/ssh behaviour). Cheap first step: reproduce with -count=20 -race and instrument the two values.
